newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Former Venezuelan president Perez forms new party.
newsitem.headline: Former Venezuelan president Perez forms new party.

text.p: Former Venezuelan President Carlos Andres Perez, the only Latin American leader to be ousted from office on corruption charges and then jailed, announced on Wednesday he had formed a new political party.

"I'm seeking to present a political agenda that sets the Venezuelan state on a true march to modernity ... a true opposition party," Perez told reporters as he outlined the latest stage of his political resurrection campaign.

Details on whether his new party, the Movement for Openness and National Participation, would field candidates in the 1998 presidential elections are to be released at the party's formal launch on Thursday, he said.
The party would allow him to "rescue" the grassroots membership of Democratic Action (AD), Perez said of the party he helped form in 1946 but that expelled him 50 years later.
Perez, 73, was forced out of office in May 1993, just eight months short of completing his second five-year mandate, on charges of misusing state funds.

After serving more than two years of house arrest in September 1996, he was stripped of the lifelong Senate position awarded former presidents and kicked out by the party he had led to two election wins.
Now Perez, backed by members of his former Cabinet, has his political sights set on regaining the Senate seat for his birth state Tachira in western Venezuela.
"I'm going to teach those that took my rightful position away a lesson," he said.
